dedupe_keys.name: rancor microworld simplified nuclear power plant simulator for process control research

description: The Rancor Microworld is a simplified nuclear power plant simulator for studying process control and operator performance. It was developed at Idaho National Laboratory by Thomas Ulrich, Ronald Boring and Roger Lew with sponsorship from the DOE Office of Nuclear Energy. It represents a pressurised light water reactor with simplified core physics and a secondary Rankine cycle turbine and generator; operators move control rods to change reactivity and output through a digital human-machine interface, aiming to maximise profit. It supports multi-unit operation like small modular reactor plants and faults on components for training scenarios such as reactor and turbine trips, and it logs process parameters, control inputs and events, gives situation awareness probes and connects to eye tracking. The method is location-independent. DOE CODE lists it as closed-source software in C# with Windows Presentation Foundation on .NET, released September 2018, with access by contacting INL. Caveats: the physics is deliberately simplified for human factors research, not plant licensing. Simulation uses are operator training and emergency response studies.
